claims.text: Combining DFT-trained machine-learned interatomic potentials with CALPHAD liquid-phase modeling can accurately and efficiently predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloys.
The workflow predicts melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, and volume change on melting.
CrMoNbTaW is an example of an equiatomic five-component refractory HEA that is solid under ambient conditions.
Moment tensor potentials are an example of ML-trained interatomic potentials suitable for the proposed workflow.
The intended composition space consists of equiatomic five-element alloys selected from refractory transition metals.
A temperature interval of 300–3000 K covers the melting transitions relevant to the target alloy family.
ML interatomic potentials capture complex many-body interactions in both the solid and liquid phases.
The ML potentials provide sufficiently accurate energetic and volumetric data for CALPHAD parameter optimization.
ML potentials can provide DFT-level cohesive and volumetric data for hundreds of liquid configurations.
Data generated by ML potentials allow CALPHAD liquid models to be calibrated without extensive experimental measurements.
The calibrated CALPHAD model can predict melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamics across the target HEA family.
Melting temperatures will be predicted within ±50 K of experiment.
Fusion enthalpies will be predicted within ±0.1 kJ mol⁻¹-atom of experiment.
Melting volume changes will be predicted within ±0.1 cm³ mol⁻¹ of experiment.
Each alloy can be calculated in less than 24 hours on a mid-range computing cluster.
Typical standalone CALPHAD or direct DFT molecular dynamics has errors of at least 100 K in melting temperature, 0.2 kJ mol⁻¹-atom in fusion enthalpy, and 0.2 cm³ mol⁻¹ in melting volume change.
Typical standalone CALPHAD or direct DFT molecular-dynamics calculations require more than five days per alloy.

The approach is presently applicable only to equiatomic five-component refractory HEAs and is not validated for non-equiatomic, non-refractory, volatile-element, or light-element-containing alloys such as Al-bearing alloys.
The model relies on a training set of approximately 20 HEA compositions, and extrapolation beyond that set may produce larger errors.
Failure on more than half of a blind ten-alloy validation set, using the stated error thresholds for melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, or melting volume change, would falsify the hypothesis.
